title: The Principle of Complementarity in Quantum Mechanics
text:
Quantum particles, such as photons and electrons, do not exclusively exhibit either wave or particle characteristics. Instead, they demonstrate a duality, meaning that the full description of their behavior requires both descriptions to be accounted for. This concept is formalized through Niels Bohr’s principle of complementarity.

The experiment performed by observing these entities dictates which aspect—wave or particle—is manifest. When measured in an interference pattern, wave properties are revealed; conversely, when observed with localized detection points, the discrete, corpuscular nature becomes evident. It is recognized that these two descriptions are mutually exclusive yet equally necessary for a complete understanding of physical reality at the quantum level.

This inherent duality underscores the limits of classical intuition regarding matter and energy, suggesting that observation itself fundamentally influences the measured state of the system.
